scenario: 支付平台要在 <50ms p95 内给每笔交易打分，既要抓单笔欺诈，又要抓多账号协同作案的欺诈团伙(fraud ring)。
scenario_en: A payments platform must score each transaction within <50ms p95, catching both individual fraud and coordinated multi-account fraud rings.
q: 生产级欺诈检测为什么不是单一模型，而是三组件架构？
q_en: Why is production fraud detection a three-component architecture rather than one model?
why: 三组件是 defense-in-depth：规则引擎零推理成本秒挡已知坏模式，GBT 用毫秒级 CPU 给单笔交易打分，GraphSAGE 抓 GBT 看不见的跨账号团伙。单个模型既扛不住 <50ms 又覆盖不了这三种互补信号。
why_en: The three components form defense-in-depth: a rule engine instantly blocks known patterns at zero inference cost, GBTs score single transactions in milliseconds on CPU, and GraphSAGE catches cross-account rings the GBT can't see.

flowchart TB R["规则引擎
已知模式·零推理"] --> D["批准/拒绝/复核"] G["GBT
单笔表格打分"] --> D S["GraphSAGE
跨账号团伙"] -.嵌入作特征.-> G
options: 单个大型深度模型端到端打分，靠模型容量同时覆盖单笔欺诈和团伙欺诈，省去多组件运维
规则引擎(挡已知模式)+ 梯度提升树(单笔打分)+ GraphSAGE(抓团伙)三层互补盲区
只用规则引擎穷举所有已知欺诈模式，规则写得够多够勤就完全不需要任何 ML
只用 GraphSAGE 图模型，认为它既能抓单笔又能抓团伙，一个图模型全包
options_en: One large deep model scores end to end, using capacity to cover both individual and ring fraud, avoiding multi-component ops.
A rule engine (known patterns) + gradient boosted trees (single-transaction scoring) + GraphSAGE (ring detection), covering each other's blind spots.
Just a rule engine enumerating every known fraud pattern; with enough rules, kept fresh, you need no ML at all.
Just GraphSAGE, assuming one graph model can handle both individual transactions and rings.
optionExplanations: 一个深度模型 10-20ms 推理就吃满预算，还得 GPU，且在稀有欺诈的表格数据上通常打不过树模型。
对；规则、GBT、图模型三种信号各补对方盲区，是延迟预算下同时抓单笔与团伙的标准解法。
规则只能覆盖已知、能显式写出的模式，抓不到会随数据演化的新型行为欺诈，仍需会学习的 ML。
GraphSAGE 的嵌入要异步预计算、有 5-15 分钟滞后，不能实时给每一笔单独打分，扛不了热路径。
optionExplanations_en: One deep model's 10-20ms inference eats the whole budget, needs a GPU, and usually loses to trees on rare-positive tabular data.
Correct — rules, GBTs, and a graph model each cover the others' gaps, the standard way to catch both individual and ring fraud under a latency budget.
Rules only cover known, explicitly-writable patterns and miss evolving behavioral fraud, so learning ML is still needed.
GraphSAGE embeddings are precomputed asynchronously with a 5-15 min lag, so they can't score every single transaction in real time on the hot path.

termDefinitions.meaning: 梯度提升树：顺序建树、每棵纠正前面误差的集成模型，表格数据的主力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GBT (Gradient Boosted Trees) is an ensemble that builds trees sequentially, each correcting prior errors, the workhorse for tabular data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种归纳式图神经网络，聚合邻居特征生成节点嵌入，用来抓账号间的团伙结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GraphSAGE (Graph SAmple and aggreGatE) is an inductive graph neural network that aggregates neighbor features into node embeddings to detect ring structure.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多层各自独立的防线，每层覆盖别层的盲点，任一层失效仍有兜底。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Defense-in-depth stacks independent layers so each covers the others' blind spots and one failing layer still leaves a fallback.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多个账号协同作案、常共享设备或支付工具的欺诈网络。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A fraud ring is a network of accounts committing fraud together, often sharing devices or payment instruments.

scenario: 欺诈特征是表格数据(交易金额、MCC 类别、二元风控标志)，正样本极稀有(<0.1%)，要在 <50ms 内 CPU 出分、还要能向监管解释拒付原因。
scenario_en: Fraud features are tabular (amount, MCC category, binary flags), positives are rare (<0.1%), scoring must run on CPU within <50ms, and declines must be explainable to regulators.
q: 实时表格欺诈打分该选梯度提升树还是深度神经网络？
q_en: For real-time tabular fraud scoring, GBTs or a deep neural network?
why: 选 GBT：顺序建树在 <0.1% 稀有正类上依然有效，CPU 1-5ms 出分不用 GPU，原生吃异构表格特征，还自带特征重要性能向监管解释拒付。深度网络要 GPU、要 one-hot/归一化，且在表格数据上通常不占优。
why_en: Choose GBTs: sequential boosting stays effective on the <0.1% positive class, scores in 1-5ms on CPU with no GPU, natively ingests heterogeneous tabular features, and exposes feature importance to explain declines.
tradeoff: GBT(毫秒级 CPU、原生表格、可解释) vs DNN(需 GPU、要特征预处理、黑箱)
whenOtherWins: 若输入是高维非结构化数据(原始文本、图像、行为序列)且有 GPU 预算，深度模型的表示学习才反超 GBT。
options: 深度神经网络(MLP)：容量大，认为它在表格数据上也一定更准，值得为它上 GPU 集群
逻辑回归：线性系数最可解释，为了合规宁可牺牲一截召回也坚持只用它
梯度提升树(XGBoost/LightGBM)：CPU 毫秒出分、原生吃表格特征、自带特征重要性
随机森林：同为树模型且各树独立并行，认为精度天然高于顺序提升的 GBT
options_en: A deep neural network (MLP): high capacity, assumed more accurate even on tabular data, worth standing up a GPU cluster.
Logistic regression: linear coefficients are the most interpretable, so stick with it even at a real recall cost for compliance.
Gradient boosted trees (XGBoost/LightGBM): millisecond CPU scoring, native tabular features, built-in feature importance.
Random forest: also trees, but independent parallel trees, assumed inherently more accurate than sequential boosting.
optionExplanations: 深度模型在表格数据上通常打不过 GBT，还要 GPU 和 one-hot/归一化预处理，10-20ms 推理也吃满延迟预算。
逻辑回归线性、表达力弱抓不住特征交互；可解释不该以牺牲欺诈召回为代价。
对；GBT 在稀有正类上有效、CPU 1-5ms 出分、原生表格特征、特征重要性可向监管解释拒付，四项全中。
随机森林可并行但精度通常不及顺序纠错的 boosting，且 ~8ms 推理比 LightGBM 慢。
optionExplanations_en: Deep models usually lose to GBTs on tabular data, need a GPU and one-hot/normalization, and 10-20ms inference eats the latency budget.
Logistic regression is linear and weak at feature interactions; interpretability shouldn't cost fraud recall.
Correct — GBTs stay effective on rare positives, score in 1-5ms on CPU, ingest tabular features natively, and expose feature importance for declines.
Random forest parallelizes but usually trails error-correcting boosting on accuracy, and ~8ms inference is slower than LightGBM.

termDefinitions.meaning: 顺序建树、每棵纠正前面误差的树集成，表格数据主力(XGBoost/LightGBM)。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GBT (Gradient Boosted Trees) sequentially builds trees each correcting prior errors, the tabular workhorse (XGBoost/LightGBM).

termDefinitions.meaning: 商户类别码，标记交易商户类型的类别型特征。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MCC (Merchant Category Code) is a categorical feature tagging the merchant type of a transaction.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多层感知机，最基础的前馈深度网络，需数值化输入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MLP (Multi-Layer Perceptron) is the basic feedforward deep network, requiring numeric inputs.

scenario: LightGBM 在 CPU 上单笔交易推理约 1-5ms，全程不需要 GPU。
scenario_en: LightGBM scores one transaction in roughly 1-5ms on CPU, with no GPU needed.
q: 「GBT 推理 1-5ms 且不用 GPU」这个数字对架构意味着什么？
q_en: What does 'GBT inference in 1-5ms with no GPU' imply for the architecture?
why: 这是给定的经验量级(不是公式推导)：1-5ms 说明模型推理不是 50ms 预算里的瓶颈，可以在纯 CPU 上水平扩展、不必为 GPU 集群买单；真正吃预算的是特征库查询(~8ms)。
why_en: This is an empirical order of magnitude, not a formula: 1-5ms means inference is not the bottleneck in the 50ms budget, so you scale horizontally on plain CPU and skip a GPU cluster, while feature lookups (~8ms) dominate.
options: 说明必须上 GPU 集群才能压到 1-5ms，模型推理就是关键路径上的主要瓶颈
1-5ms 是给定经验量级：推理不占 50ms 预算大头，纯 CPU 就能水平扩展
说明可以换成容量更大的深度网络，反正推理已经很快、预算还剩很多
1-5ms 是要背下来的硬性指标，考点就是把这个数字本身记牢
options_en: It means a GPU cluster is required to reach 1-5ms, and model inference is the main critical-path bottleneck.
1-5ms is a given empirical magnitude: inference isn't the bulk of the 50ms budget, so plain CPUs scale out fine.
It means you can swap in a much bigger deep network, since inference is already fast and budget is left over.
1-5ms is a hard number to memorize; the point is simply recalling the value itself.

termDefinitions.meaning: 梯度提升树，CPU 上毫秒级推理、无需 GPU。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GBT (Gradient Boosted Trees) run millisecond CPU inference with no GPU.

termDefinitions.meaning: 95% 的请求延迟低于这个值，衡量尾部延迟而非平均值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: p95 latency is the value below which 95% of requests fall, measuring tail latency rather than the mean.

optionExplanations: 推理已经是 1-5ms 的 CPU 量级，根本不需要 GPU 集群，这个选项把因果搞反了。
对；这个量级确认推理早就不是瓶颈，真正该盯的是约 8ms 的特征查询那一段。
推理快不等于该加大模型，换更大网络只会重新吃满延迟预算，没必要。
这里的重点是数字背后的架构含义，不是让你死记一个毫秒数。
optionExplanations_en: Inference already runs at 1-5ms on CPU; a GPU cluster isn't needed, so this gets the causality backwards.
Correct — this magnitude confirms inference isn't what eats the 50ms; watch the ~8ms lookup step instead.
Fast inference isn't a reason to scale up the model; a bigger network would just re-eat the latency budget.
The point is the architectural implication of the number, not memorizing a millisecond figure.

scenario: 欺诈特征混杂：类别型 MCC、连续型金额、二元风控标志，全都要喂进模型。
scenario_en: Fraud features are mixed: categorical MCC, continuous amount, binary risk flags, all fed to the model.
q: 为什么 GBT 能直接吃这些异构特征，而深度网络要额外预处理？
q_en: Why can GBTs ingest these heterogeneous features directly while deep nets need preprocessing?
why: 树的分裂在每个特征上找阈值或分组，天然处理类别、连续、二元的混合，不用 one-hot 或归一化。深度网络要求数值化输入，得先 one-hot 编码类别、归一化连续值，多一层预处理还会维度膨胀。
why_en: Tree splits find a threshold or grouping on each feature, natively handling categorical, continuous, and binary together with no one-hot or normalization, whereas deep nets require numeric inputs, adding a one-hot/normalization step and dimension blow-up.
options: GBT 内部也会自动做 one-hot 和归一化，本质与深度网络的预处理没区别
深度网络能直接吃类别/连续混合，反而是 GBT 需要先归一化
两者都要求先把类别特征 embedding 成向量才能训练
树分裂在每个特征上找阈值或分组，原生处理类别+连续+二元，无需 one-hot 或归一化
options_en: GBTs internally also do one-hot and normalization, so it's no different from deep-net preprocessing.
Deep nets ingest mixed categorical/continuous directly; it's actually GBTs that need normalization first.
Both require embedding categorical features into vectors before training.
Tree splits find a threshold or grouping per feature, natively handling categorical + continuous + binary with no one-hot or normalization.
optionExplanations: GBT 的分裂直接在原始特征上比较，不需要 one-hot/归一化这类深度网络才要的预处理。
说反了：深度网络才要数值化输入，GBT 原生就能吃类别与连续混合。
embedding 是深度网络处理高基数类别的做法，树模型不需要它就能分裂类别。
对；树按特征找分裂点，异构混合直接可用，这正是它在表格数据上省事又强的原因。
optionExplanations_en: GBT splits compare on raw features and don't need the one-hot/normalization that deep nets require.
Backwards: deep nets need numeric inputs, while GBTs natively ingest mixed categorical and continuous.
Embedding is how deep nets handle high-cardinality categories; trees split categories without it.
Correct — trees find split points per feature, so heterogeneous mixes work directly, which is why they're both easy and strong on tabular data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把类别特征展开成一堆 0/1 列，深度网络吃类别时的常见预处理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: One-hot encoding expands a categorical feature into many 0/1 columns, a common preprocessing step for deep nets.

termDefinitions.meaning: 商户类别码，一种类别型交易特征。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MCC (Merchant Category Code) is a categorical transaction feature for merchant type.

scenario: 监管要求：拒付一笔交易时，要能解释「为什么这笔被判为欺诈」。
scenario_en: Regulators require that when a transaction is declined, you can explain why it was flagged as fraud.
q: GBT 的哪个特性满足这条监管可解释性要求？
q_en: Which GBT property satisfies this regulatory interpretability requirement?
why: GBT 自带特征重要性(每个特征对分裂增益的贡献)，能指出哪些特征把这笔交易推向欺诈，可审计地解释拒付。一个不透明的欺诈概率满足不了「解释拒付」的合规要求。
why_en: GBTs come with feature importance (each feature's contribution to split gain), so you can name which features pushed a transaction toward fraud and auditably justify the decline, which an opaque probability cannot.
options: GBT 自带特征重要性，能指出哪些特征把这笔交易推向欺诈，可审计地解释拒付
GBT 输出的是黑箱概率，可解释性和深度网络一样差，要另训解释模型
GBT 靠更快的推理速度满足可解释性(速度快=透明)
GBT 参数量小所以自动可解释，与特征重要性无关
options_en: GBTs expose feature importance, naming which features pushed the transaction toward fraud to auditably justify the decline.
GBTs output a black-box probability, as opaque as a deep net, needing a separate explainer model.
GBTs satisfy interpretability through faster inference (fast = transparent).
GBTs are auto-interpretable due to small parameter count, unrelated to feature importance.
optionExplanations: 对；特征重要性把「哪些特征驱动了这次判定」摊开，监管要的可审计解释正落在这里。
GBT 恰恰比深度网络透明，特征重要性天然可读，无需事后再训解释模型。
推理快是延迟属性，跟能不能解释一次判定毫无关系。
可解释来自树结构与特征重要性，不是参数少就自动可解释。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — feature importance lays out which features drove the decision, exactly the auditable explanation regulators want.
GBTs are more transparent than deep nets; feature importance is readable, needing no post-hoc explainer.
Fast inference is a latency property, unrelated to explaining a decision.
Interpretability comes from tree structure and feature importance, not from having few parameters.

termDefinitions.meaning: 衡量每个特征对模型分裂增益/预测的贡献，用来解释一次判定。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Feature importance measures each feature's contribution to split gain or prediction, used to explain a decision.

scenario: 欺诈是极端不平衡问题：正样本(欺诈)常 <0.1% 的交易量。
scenario_en: Fraud is extremely imbalanced: positive (fraud) samples are often <0.1% of volume.
q: boosting「顺序建树、每棵纠正前面错误」为什么特别适合这种稀有正类？
q_en: Why does boosting's 'sequential trees, each correcting prior errors' suit this rare positive class?
why: boosting 顺序建树，每棵新树重点拟合前面分错的样本——多是被淹没的稀有欺诈，逐步把弱学习器叠成强学习器。这种「聚焦难例」机制正好放大 <0.1% 的欺诈信号，比一次性拟合更能抓住稀有正类。
why_en: Boosting builds trees sequentially, each new tree focusing on previously misclassified samples — often the drowned-out rare fraud — stacking weak learners into a strong one, which amplifies the <0.1% fraud signal better than a single fit.
options: boosting 并行训练很多独立树再投票，靠数量压过稀有类噪声
boosting 随机丢弃大部分多数类样本来强行平衡，本质是欠采样
顺序建树、每棵新树聚焦前面分错的样本(多为稀有欺诈)，弱学习器叠成强学习器
boosting 只是把逻辑回归跑很多遍取平均，和树无关
options_en: Boosting trains many independent trees in parallel and votes, using count to overpower rare-class noise.
Boosting randomly drops most majority samples to force balance — essentially undersampling.
Sequential trees, each new one focusing on prior misclassifications (often rare fraud), stacking weak learners into a strong one.
Boosting just runs logistic regression many times and averages, unrelated to trees.
optionExplanations: 并行独立投票是随机森林(bagging)的做法，boosting 恰恰是顺序、后一棵依赖前一棵。
boosting 不靠丢样本平衡，它靠对分错样本加权/聚焦，稀有欺诈正好被重点学习。
对；聚焦难例让每一轮都补上被淹没的欺诈，稀有正类的信号被逐步放大。
boosting 的弱学习器一般就是树，不是重复的逻辑回归取平均。
optionExplanations_en: Parallel independent voting is random forest (bagging); boosting is sequential with each tree depending on the last.
Boosting doesn't balance by dropping samples; it reweights/focuses on misclassifications, so rare fraud gets emphasized.
Correct — focusing on hard cases lets each round pick up drowned-out fraud, amplifying the rare positive signal.
Boosting's weak learners are typically trees, not repeated logistic regressions averaged.

termDefinitions.meaning: 顺序训练弱学习器，每个纠正前一个的错误，叠成强学习器的集成方法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Boosting sequentially trains weak learners, each correcting the previous one's errors, into a strong ensemble.

termDefinitions.term: rare positive class / 稀有正类
termDefinitions.meaning: 正样本占比极低(如欺诈 <0.1%)的不平衡分类问题。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A rare positive class is an imbalanced problem where positives are a tiny fraction (e.g. fraud <0.1%).

scenario: 在 50ms 预算下调 GBT，你在 LightGBM 和 XGBoost 的树生长策略之间权衡。
scenario_en: Tuning a GBT under a 50ms budget, you weigh LightGBM's and XGBoost's tree-growth strategies.
q: LightGBM 的 leaf-wise 与 XGBoost 的 level-wise 生长有何不同，对延迟意味着什么？
q_en: How do LightGBM's leaf-wise and XGBoost's level-wise growth differ, and what does it mean for latency?
why: LightGBM 按叶(leaf-wise)生长，每次分裂增益最大的叶，更贪心、常用更少的树就达标、推理更快；XGBoost 按层(level-wise)每层全展开，树更平衡更稳但略慢。延迟敏感的欺诈打分常选 LightGBM。
why_en: LightGBM grows leaf-wise, splitting the highest-gain leaf so it reaches target accuracy with fewer trees and scores faster; XGBoost grows level-wise, expanding every level into more balanced, robust but slightly slower trees, so latency-sensitive scoring often picks LightGBM.
tradeoff: LightGBM leaf-wise(更贪心、推理快、易过拟合) vs XGBoost level-wise(层展开、更平衡更稳、略慢)
options: leaf-wise 和 level-wise 只是命名习惯不同，两者生长方式和推理速度其实完全一样
LightGBM 按叶生长、少树即达标推理更快；XGBoost 按层生长、更平衡稳但略慢
XGBoost 按叶生长所以推理更快，LightGBM 按层生长所以更慢，正好和实际相反
两者都必须用 GPU 才能达到毫秒级出分，差别只在显存占用的多少
options_en: leaf-wise and level-wise are just naming conventions; growth and inference speed are actually identical.
LightGBM grows leaf-wise, fewer trees and faster scoring; XGBoost grows level-wise, more balanced and robust but slower.
XGBoost grows leaf-wise so it's faster, LightGBM grows level-wise so it's slower — exactly the reverse of reality.
Both need a GPU to reach millisecond scoring; the only difference is how much memory they use.
optionExplanations: 两者生长策略确实不同，导致树形和推理速度不同，不是同一回事。
对；代价是 leaf-wise 深而不平衡、更容易过拟合，小数据集要靠 num_leaves 和最小样本数压住。
说反了：leaf-wise 是 LightGBM、更快，level-wise 是 XGBoost、略慢。
两者都能在 CPU 上毫秒级推理，不是必须 GPU，差别在生长策略而非显存。
optionExplanations_en: Their growth strategies genuinely differ, driving different tree shape and speed — not the same thing.
Correct — the cost is that leaf-wise trees go deep and unbalanced and overfit more easily, so cap num_leaves and min samples on small data.
Backwards: leaf-wise is LightGBM (faster) and level-wise is XGBoost (slower).
Both run millisecond CPU inference without a GPU; the difference is growth strategy, not memory.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每次只分裂当前增益最大的叶子，树更不平衡、常用更少的树达标、推理更快(LightGBM)。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Leaf-wise growth splits the single highest-gain leaf each time, giving less balanced trees that hit target accuracy with fewer iterations and score faster (LightGBM).

termDefinitions.meaning: 逐层把所有叶子一起分裂，树更平衡更稳但更重、推理略慢(XGBoost)。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Level-wise growth splits all leaves of a level together, giving more balanced, robust but heavier, slightly slower trees (XGBoost).

scenario: GBT 逐笔独立打分：15 个账号共用同一台设备指纹和 IP，每笔单看都正常，于是全部放行。
scenario_en: GBTs score each transaction independently: 15 accounts share one device fingerprint and IP, each looks normal alone, so all pass.
q: GBT「逐笔独立评估」漏掉了什么，后果链是什么？
q_en: What does GBT's independent per-transaction scoring miss, and what is the consequence chain?
why: GBT 只看单笔交易的特征、不看账号之间的连接，所以共享设备/IP 的团伙每笔单看都正常→全部放行→协同欺诈得逞。要补上图模型(GraphSAGE)从网络结构里发现这种密集互连。
why_en: GBTs see only a transaction's own features, not links between accounts, so a ring sharing a device/IP looks normal per transaction → all pass → coordinated fraud succeeds, which is why a graph model (GraphSAGE) is added to spot the dense interconnection.
diagram:
flowchart TB
  D["同一设备指纹+IP"] --- A1["账号1"]
  D --- A2["账号2"]
  D --- A3["...账号15"]
  A1 -.单看正常.-> P["GBT 逐笔放行"]
  A2 -.单看正常.-> P
  A3 -.单看正常.-> P
options: 没有后果，GBT 逐笔打分已经足够，共享设备自然会体现在单笔特征里
会让 GBT 推理变慢，本质上是个吞吐性能问题，与召回率无关
会导致 GBT 过拟合多数类，需要补更多正样本重新训练
看不到账号间连接→共享设备的团伙每笔都被放行→协同欺诈得逞
options_en: No consequence; per-transaction GBT scoring suffices, and shared devices naturally show up in single-transaction features.
It makes GBT inference slower — fundamentally a throughput problem, unrelated to recall.
It makes the GBT overfit the majority class, so you need more positive samples and a retrain.
No visibility into account links → a ring sharing a device passes every time → coordinated fraud succeeds.
optionExplanations: 共享设备本身可以是一个特征，但一堆账号之间的连接结构单笔看不到，团伙照样溜过去。
这不是速度问题，是覆盖盲区问题：逐笔模型压根看不到跨账号结构。
过拟合是训练问题，与「看不看得到账号间连接」这个结构盲区无关。
对；补法是把邻居聚合出的嵌入当额外特征喂回 GBT，而不是替换掉 GBT。
optionExplanations_en: A shared device can be a feature, but the link structure among many accounts is invisible per transaction, so the ring slips through.
It's not a speed issue but a coverage blind spot: a per-transaction model can't see cross-account structure.
Overfitting is a training issue, unrelated to the structural blind spot of not seeing account links.
Correct — the fix feeds neighbor-aggregated embeddings back into the GBT as extra features rather than replacing the GBT.

termDefinitions.meaning: 由设备特征拼出的近似唯一标识，用来发现多账号共用同一设备。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A device fingerprint is a near-unique identifier built from device attributes, used to spot multiple accounts sharing one device.

scenario: GraphSAGE 跑在一张「实体图」上，图里的账号需要先被连成网络。
scenario_en: GraphSAGE runs on an 'entity graph' where accounts must first be linked into a network.
q: 欺诈实体图里，账号是靠什么被连起来的？
q_en: In the fraud entity graph, what links accounts together?
why: 账号通过共享实体连边：同一设备指纹、同一 IP、同一支付工具(卡/银行账户)。这些共享揭示单笔模型看不到的密集互连——一堆账号共用一台设备，就是团伙的强信号。
why_en: Accounts are linked by shared entities: the same device fingerprint, IP, or payment instrument (card/bank account), revealing dense interconnection a per-transaction model can't see — many accounts on one device is a strong ring signal.
options: 靠账号注册时间接近来连边：同一天注册的账号彼此相连
靠交易金额相似来连边：金额落在同一区间的账号相连
靠共享实体连边：同设备指纹、同 IP、同支付工具
靠账号名字拼写相似来连边：编辑距离小的账号相连
options_en: Linked by close registration times: accounts registered the same day connect.
Linked by similar transaction amounts: accounts in the same amount band connect.
Linked by shared entities: same device fingerprint, IP, or payment instrument.
Linked by similar account-name spelling: accounts with small edit distance connect.
optionExplanations: 注册时间接近噪声大、误连一片正常用户，不是团伙的可靠连边依据。
金额相似跨大量正常交易都成立，连出来的图无区分度。
对；共享设备/IP/支付工具是团伙复用资源的直接证据，连出的密集子图正是欺诈网络。
名字拼写相似既易伪造又误连，不能作为图的边。
optionExplanations_en: Close registration times are noisy and wrongly link many normal users — not a reliable ring edge.
Similar amounts hold across many normal transactions, giving a non-discriminative graph.
Correct — shared devices/IPs/payment instruments are direct evidence of resource reuse, and the dense subgraph they form is the fraud network.
Name-spelling similarity is easy to fake and wrongly links accounts, unfit as a graph edge.

termDefinitions.meaning: 以账号为节点、共享设备/IP/支付工具为边的图，用来暴露团伙结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An entity graph has accounts as nodes and shared devices/IPs/payment instruments as edges, exposing ring structure.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用于付款的卡或银行账户，多账号共用同一支付工具是团伙线索。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A payment instrument is the card or bank account used to pay; multiple accounts sharing one is a ring clue.

scenario: 要抓「欺诈团伙」：多个账号通过共享设备、IP、支付工具相互连接，形成 GBT 看不见的密集互连。
scenario_en: You must catch fraud rings: accounts interlinked via shared devices, IPs, and payment instruments in dense clusters invisible to the GBT.
q: 抓这种网络级欺诈团伙该上什么模型，为什么？
q_en: Which model catches this network-level ring fraud, and why?
why: 用 GraphSAGE 这类图神经网络：它在实体图上聚合邻居特征，把「账号周围的连接结构」压成嵌入，正好暴露单笔模型看不见的密集互连团伙。GBT 逐笔独立，天然抓不到跨账号结构。
why_en: Use a graph neural network like GraphSAGE: it aggregates neighbor features on the entity graph, compressing an account's surrounding structure into an embedding that exposes dense rings a per-transaction model misses.
tradeoff: 图模型(抓跨账号结构但要建图+异步算嵌入) vs 逐笔模型(简单低延迟但盲于团伙)
whenOtherWins: 若欺诈基本是孤立的单账号行为、账号之间没有可建图的共享实体，图模型收益不大，GBT 逐笔打分就够。
options: 再训一个容量更大的 GBT，喂更多单笔交易特征，靠模型容量抓出团伙
用规则引擎穷举所有共享设备的组合，规则写得够多就能覆盖团伙
用 GraphSAGE：在实体图上聚合邻居特征，把连接结构压成嵌入
用无监督聚类把相似交易分组，某组一旦变大就整组判为欺诈
options_en: Train a bigger GBT and feed it more single-transaction features; capacity alone will catch rings.
Use a rule engine enumerating every shared-device combination; enough rules will cover rings.
Use GraphSAGE: aggregate neighbor features on the entity graph, compressing link structure into an embedding.
Use unsupervised clustering on similar transactions and flag a whole cluster once it grows.
optionExplanations: GBT 再大也只看单笔特征，看不到账号间连接，加特征补不了结构盲区。
组合爆炸且共享模式会变，规则穷举既写不全又易过时，抓不住演化的团伙。
对；图模型聚合邻居把连接结构编码进嵌入，密集互连的团伙一目了然，是网络级欺诈的正解。
按金额聚类误伤大批正常相似交易，无区分度，也不利用账号间的真实连接。
optionExplanations_en: A bigger GBT still sees only single-transaction features, not account links; more features can't fix the structural blind spot.
Combinations explode and sharing patterns shift, so enumerated rules are incomplete and stale, missing evolving rings.
Correct — a graph model encodes link structure into embeddings, making dense rings visible, the right answer for network-level fraud.
Clustering by amount wrongly groups many normal transactions, is non-discriminative, and ignores real account links.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在图上通过聚合邻居信息学习节点表示的模型家族，GraphSAGE 是其一。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A GNN (Graph Neural Network) learns node representations by aggregating neighbor information on a graph; GraphSAGE is one.

termDefinitions.meaning: 归纳式图神经网络，聚合采样到的邻居特征生成节点嵌入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GraphSAGE (Graph SAmple and aggreGatE) is an inductive GNN that aggregates sampled neighbor features into node embeddings.

scenario: 新账号持续不断注册进来，打分时图里天天出现训练时没见过的节点。
scenario_en: New accounts register continuously, so scoring time constantly sees nodes unseen at training.
q: 为什么欺诈图模型要用归纳式的 GraphSAGE，而不是转导式的 GCN？
q_en: Why use inductive GraphSAGE rather than transductive GCN for the fraud graph?
why: GraphSAGE 是归纳式：学的是「如何聚合邻居特征」的函数，遇到训练时没见过的新账号也能现场算出嵌入。GCN 是转导式，嵌入绑定训练时的固定图，新节点得整图重训。欺诈里新账号源源不断，必须用归纳式。
why_en: GraphSAGE is inductive: it learns a function for aggregating neighbor features, so it computes embeddings on the fly for accounts unseen at training, while GCN is transductive with embeddings tied to the fixed training graph, needing a full retrain for new nodes.
tradeoff: 归纳式 GraphSAGE(泛化到新节点、可在线) vs 转导式 GCN(绑定固定图、新节点需重训)
options: GCN 也是归纳式，两者对新出现的节点都能直接算出嵌入，没有区别
GraphSAGE 学邻居聚合函数，新账号现场可算嵌入；GCN 绑定训练图要重训
GraphSAGE 更慢但更准，选它只是为了精度提升，与新节点完全无关
GCN 才是归纳式、GraphSAGE 是转导式，所以新账号多的场景应该选 GCN
options_en: GCN is inductive too; both compute embeddings for newly appearing nodes directly, so there's no difference.
GraphSAGE learns a neighbor-aggregation function, so new accounts get embeddings on the fly; GCN is tied to the training graph and needs retraining.
GraphSAGE is slower but more accurate; you pick it purely for accuracy, unrelated to new nodes.
GCN is the inductive one and GraphSAGE the transductive one, so pick GCN when new accounts keep arriving.
optionExplanations: GCN 是转导式，新节点不重训就没有嵌入，两者对新节点的处理完全不同。
对；归纳式学的是聚合函数而非固定嵌入表，正好匹配新账号不断出现、要在线算分的欺诈场景。
关键不是快慢，而是归纳式能给训练时没见过的新账号算嵌入，这才是选它的原因。
说反了：GraphSAGE 归纳式、GCN 转导式，欺诈要选归纳式的 GraphSAGE。
optionExplanations_en: GCN is transductive; without retraining, new nodes have no embedding, so the two differ sharply on new nodes.
Correct — inductive learns an aggregation function, not a fixed embedding table, matching fraud where new accounts appear and must be scored online.
The point isn't speed but that inductive can embed accounts unseen at training, which is why you pick it.
Backwards: GraphSAGE is inductive and GCN transductive, so fraud picks inductive GraphSAGE.

termDefinitions.meaning: 学习一个可泛化的函数，能对训练时未见过的新节点直接生成嵌入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Inductive learning fits a generalizable function that produces embeddings for nodes unseen at training.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只对训练时图里的固定节点学嵌入，新节点需重新训练整图。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Transductive learning fixes embeddings for nodes in the training graph, requiring a retrain for new nodes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 转导式图卷积网络，嵌入绑定训练图，不便处理持续新增的节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GCN (Graph Convolutional Network) is a transductive graph model whose embeddings bind to the training graph, awkward for continuously arriving nodes.

scenario: GraphSAGE 要给每个账号算一个反映其网络位置的固定维度嵌入，喂给下游 GBT。
scenario_en: GraphSAGE must give each account a fixed-dimension embedding reflecting its network position, fed to the downstream GBT.
q: GraphSAGE 怎么把一个账号的局部网络结构变成固定维度的嵌入？
q_en: How does GraphSAGE turn an account's local network structure into a fixed-dimension embedding?
why: 它聚合该账号 1-hop(直接邻居)和 2-hop(邻居的邻居)的特征，逐层汇总成一个固定维度向量，这个嵌入编码了「账号周围连了谁、结构多密」。固定维度才能当额外特征喂进下游 GBT。
why_en: It aggregates the account's 1-hop (direct neighbors) and 2-hop (neighbors' neighbors) features, summarizing layer by layer into a fixed-length vector that encodes who it connects to and how dense the structure is, so it can feed the GBT as an extra feature.
options: 聚合 1-hop 与 2-hop 邻居特征，逐层汇总成固定维嵌入
直接把账号 ID 做 one-hot 当嵌入，完全不看任何邻居结构
把整张图所有节点特征平均成一个全局向量，所有账号共用同一个
只用账号自己的交易特征做嵌入，不聚合任何邻居信息
options_en: Aggregate 1-hop and 2-hop neighbor features, summarizing layer by layer into a fixed-dim embedding.
One-hot the account ID as its embedding, ignoring neighbor structure entirely.
Average all node features in the whole graph into one global vector shared by every account.
Use only the account's own transaction features, aggregating no neighbor information.
optionExplanations: 对；多跳邻居聚合把「周围连了谁、多密」编码进定长向量，正好捕捉团伙的局部结构。
ID one-hot 不含结构信息、维度还爆炸，学不到团伙的连接模式。
全局平均抹掉了个体差异，每个账号一样的嵌入没有区分度。
只用自身特征就退化成 GBT 的逐笔视角，看不到网络结构，等于没上图模型。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — multi-hop aggregation encodes who it connects to and how dense into a fixed vector, capturing the ring's local structure.
ID one-hot carries no structure and explodes in dimension, learning no ring connectivity.
Global averaging erases individual differences, giving every account the same, non-discriminative embedding.
Using only own features collapses back to the GBT's per-transaction view, seeing no network structure.

termDefinitions.meaning: 1-hop 是直接相连的邻居，2-hop 是邻居的邻居，越多跳看得越远。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: 1-hop neighbors are directly connected; 2-hop are neighbors of neighbors — more hops see further.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一个节点的特征与局部结构压成的固定维度向量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A node embedding is a fixed-dimension vector compressing a node's features and local structure.

scenario: 图上做 2-hop 邻居聚合很重，若放进打分热路径会加 50-200ms，直接吃光 50ms 的整个预算。
scenario_en: 2-hop neighbor aggregation on the graph is heavy; inline in the hot path it adds 50-200ms, the entire 50ms budget.
q: GraphSAGE 嵌入该怎么服务，才能既用上团伙信号又不炸延迟预算？
q_en: How should GraphSAGE embeddings be served to use the ring signal without blowing the latency budget?
why: 两趟(two-pass)：异步小批量每 5-15 分钟随图更新重算嵌入、写进特征库；打分时只做一次 KV 查询取预计算好的嵌入喂给 GBT。把 50-200ms 的重计算移出热路径，在线只留毫秒级查表。
why_en: Two passes: an async mini-batch job re-embeds every 5-15 minutes as the graph updates and writes to the feature store; scoring does a single KV lookup of the precomputed embedding for the GBT, keeping the 50-200ms recompute off the hot path.
tradeoff: 异步预计算嵌入(在线毫秒查表但有 5-15 分钟滞后) vs 实时内联聚合(最新但 +50-200ms 炸预算)
whenOtherWins: 若团伙形成极快、5-15 分钟滞后完全不可接受，且延迟预算宽松，才考虑把更轻量的实时图计算搬进热路径。
diagram:
flowchart LR GR["图更新"] --> EMB["每5-15min重算
GraphSAGE嵌入"] EMB --> FS[("特征库")] Q["打分请求"] --> KV["KV查预计算嵌入"] FS --> KV KV --> GBT["GBT打分"]
options: 打分时在热路径实时跑 2-hop 邻居聚合拿最新嵌入，反正只多几毫秒
干脆不用 GraphSAGE 嵌入，图计算太重，热路径上只保留 GBT
每次打分都对整张图重算所有账号的嵌入，再从中取本账号那一个
两趟：异步每 5-15min 重算嵌入写特征库，打分时一次 KV 查表
options_en: Run 2-hop aggregation live on the hot path at scoring time for the freshest embedding — it's only a few ms.
Just drop GraphSAGE embeddings; graph compute is too heavy, keep only the GBT on the hot path.
Recompute embeddings for every account over the whole graph on each scoring call, then take this one.
Two passes: async recompute every 5-15 min into the feature store, one KV lookup at scoring time.
optionExplanations: 内联 2-hop 聚合是 50-200ms，不是几毫秒，直接吃光整个 50ms 预算。
放弃图嵌入就丢了团伙信号，等于回到 GBT 的盲区，不是好取舍。
整图重算比单账号还贵，每次打分都做完全不可能满足 <50ms。
对；把重计算异步化、在线只留毫秒查表，是热路径用上团伙信号的标准解，代价是 5-15 分钟滞后。
optionExplanations_en: Inline 2-hop aggregation is 50-200ms, not a few ms, eating the entire 50ms budget.
Dropping embeddings loses the ring signal, back to the GBT's blind spot — a bad trade.
Recomputing the whole graph is even costlier than one account and can't meet <50ms per call.
Correct — async recompute plus a millisecond online lookup is the standard way to use ring signal on the hot path, at the cost of a 5-15 min lag.

termDefinitions.meaning: 重计算异步预跑写存储，在线只做轻量查表，把慢步骤移出热路径。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Two-pass serving precomputes the heavy step asynchronously into storage and does only a light lookup online, moving the slow work off the hot path.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按键(账号)直接取值(预计算嵌入)的毫秒级查询。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A KV (Key-Value) lookup fetches a value (the precomputed embedding) by key (the account) in milliseconds.

termDefinitions.meaning: 存放预计算特征供在线打分低延迟读取的存储系统。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A feature store holds precomputed features for low-latency reads during online scoring.

scenario: GraphSAGE 嵌入每 5-15 分钟异步重算一次，而不是实时更新。
scenario_en: GraphSAGE embeddings are re-computed asynchronously every 5-15 minutes, not in real time.
q: 「每 5-15 分钟重算嵌入」这个节奏对检测能力意味着什么？
q_en: What does the '5-15 minute re-embed cadence' imply for detection?
why: 这是工程取舍的给定节奏(不是公式推导)：它把 50-200ms 的重计算挪出热路径，代价是新形成的团伙有 5-15 分钟检测滞后——窗口内作案时嵌入还是旧的。这段缺口由实时的规则引擎兜底。
why_en: It's a chosen engineering cadence, not a formula: it moves the 50-200ms recompute off the hot path, at the cost of a 5-15 minute detection lag for new rings whose embeddings are stale within the window, a gap the real-time rule engine covers.
options: 5-15 分钟是模型的离线训练周期，和线上检测滞后完全无关
说明团伙一形成就立刻被图模型抓到，中间没有任何检测滞后
新团伙有 5-15 分钟检测滞后，窗口内用旧嵌入，缺口靠规则兜底
5-15 分钟是要背下来的硬性指标，考点就是记住这个数字本身
options_en: 5-15 min is the model's offline training cycle, unrelated to online detection lag.
It means a ring is caught by the graph model the instant it forms, with no detection lag at all.
New rings carry a 5-15 min detection lag, run on stale embeddings inside the window, and rules cover the gap.
5-15 min is a hard number to memorize; the point is recalling the value itself.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从欺诈发生到系统能察觉之间的时间差，这里由异步重算周期造成。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Detection lag is the delay between fraud occurring and the system noticing it, here caused by the async recompute cycle.

optionExplanations: 训练周期是另一回事，这里的 5-15 分钟指的是线上嵌入的重算间隔。
嵌入是异步重算的，新团伙在窗口内看到的还是旧嵌入，不可能零滞后。
对；这个节奏就是滞后窗口的来源，缺口靠规则引擎实时补上。
重点是这个节奏带来的检测滞后，不是让你背下这两个数字。
optionExplanations_en: The training cycle is a separate thing; the 5-15 min here is the online re-embed interval.
Embeddings are recomputed asynchronously, so a brand-new ring is scored on a stale embedding within that window — never zero lag.
Correct — this cadence is exactly where the lag window comes from, and the rule engine backstops that gap live.
The point is the detection lag this cadence causes, not memorizing the two numbers.

scenario: 一个刚在 5 分钟内组建、马上就作案的欺诈团伙，此刻 GraphSAGE 嵌入还是旧的、根本看不出它。
scenario_en: A ring formed within the last 5 minutes strikes immediately; its GraphSAGE embedding is still stale and doesn't reveal it.
q: 新团伙的检测滞后会漏掉这波攻击吗，架构靠什么兜底？
q_en: Will the new-ring detection lag miss this attack, and what covers it?
why: 异步嵌入有 5-15 分钟滞后→窗口内新团伙嵌入是旧的→图信号暂时失效；但规则引擎(共享设备阈值、可疑 BIN 等确定性规则)在热路径实时兜住这段缺口。这正是 defense-in-depth 让各组件互补盲区。
why_en: Async embeddings lag 5-15 min → a new ring's embedding is stale in that window → graph signal is temporarily blind; but the rule engine (shared-device thresholds, suspicious BINs) covers the gap in real time on the hot path, defense-in-depth where components cover each other.
options: 会直接漏掉，架构没有任何补救手段，只能等下一次重算
图信号暂时失效，但规则引擎用确定性规则实时兜住这段缺口
不会漏，GBT 单笔打分本来就能独立抓住刚组建的新团伙
把嵌入重算频率提到每秒一次来彻底消除滞后，代价完全可接受
options_en: It's simply missed; the architecture has no remedy and you wait for the next recompute.
Graph signal goes temporarily blind, but the rule engine covers that gap in real time with deterministic rules.
Nothing is missed; per-transaction GBT scoring already catches a freshly formed ring on its own.
Push embedding recompute to once per second to eliminate the lag entirely, at fully acceptable cost.
optionExplanations: 架构恰恰为这个缺口准备了兜底，不是无补救，纵深防御的意义就在这里。
对；某一层暂时失效时，另一层(实时规则)顶上，这就是三组件互补盲区的价值。
GBT 逐笔独立，看不到账号间连接，抓不住刚形成的团伙，正是它的盲区。
每秒整图重算成本爆炸也未必赶得上，滞后靠架构兜底而非硬提频率解决。
optionExplanations_en: The architecture is built to cover this gap, not helpless — that's the point of defense-in-depth.
Correct — when one layer is briefly blind, another (real-time rules) takes over, the value of three complementary components.
The GBT is per-transaction and can't see account links, so a just-formed ring is exactly its blind spot.
Per-second full recompute explodes cost and may still lag; the fix is architectural fallback, not brute-force frequency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 银行卡号前几位，标识发卡行；失陷/高风险 BIN 可被规则直接拦。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A BIN (Bank Identification Number) is the leading card digits identifying the issuer; compromised/high-risk BINs can be blocked by rules.

scenario: 有些交易来自受制裁国家或已知被盗的 BIN(银行卡号前缀)，判定是确定性的、根本不需要概率模型。
scenario_en: Some transactions come from sanctioned countries or known-compromised BINs (card prefixes); the decision is deterministic and needs no probabilistic model.
q: 这类「已知必拦」的交易该用什么处理，为什么不走 ML？
q_en: How should these 'known must-block' transactions be handled, and why not ML?
why: 用规则引擎确定性硬拦：受制裁国家/失陷 BIN 是布尔判定，零推理成本、即时、可审计。给它跑 ML 算概率既浪费算力，又不如显式规则可解释。
why_en: Use the rule engine to hard-block deterministically: sanctioned countries and compromised BINs are boolean checks — zero inference cost, instant, auditable — whereas running ML on them wastes compute and is less explainable than an explicit rule.
tradeoff: 规则引擎(确定性、零成本、可审计，但只覆盖已知模式) vs ML(能学新模式但有推理成本、不透明)
whenOtherWins: 当模式是模糊的、会随数据演化的(如新型行为欺诈)，确定性规则写不出来，就该交给会从数据学习的 GBT。
options: 用规则引擎确定性硬拦：布尔判定、零推理成本、即时且可审计
交给 GBT 算欺诈概率，概率高再拦，统一走一条路径最简单
交给 GraphSAGE 先看它是不是团伙的一部分再决定
先放行并记录，等异步嵌入更新后再回溯拦截
options_en: Hard-block with the rule engine: a boolean check, zero inference cost, instant and auditable.
Send it to the GBT for a fraud probability and block if high — one unified path is simplest.
Send it to GraphSAGE to check ring membership first, then decide.
Approve and log first, then retro-block once the async embedding updates.
optionExplanations: 对；已知坏模式是布尔判定，规则零成本即时拦，还能审计，比给它跑 ML 更省更透明。
对已经确定要拦的交易还去跑 ML，白付一次推理成本，且概率不如显式规则可解释。
图模型有异步滞后、也不针对制裁/失陷 BIN 这类确定性名单，用它属于杀鸡用牛刀且慢。
已知必拦的却先放行，等回溯就晚了，钱已经出去，风险敞口不可接受。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — a known-bad pattern is a boolean check the rule engine blocks instantly at zero cost and auditably, cheaper and clearer than ML.
Running ML on an already-certain block wastes an inference and a probability is less explainable than an explicit rule.
The graph model lags asynchronously and isn't aimed at deterministic sanction/compromised-BIN lists, so it's overkill and slow.
Approving a must-block first and retro-blocking is too late — the money is gone; the exposure is unacceptable.

termDefinitions.meaning: 银行卡号前缀，标识发卡行；失陷 BIN 属于确定性拦截名单。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A BIN (Bank Identification Number) is the card prefix identifying the issuer; compromised BINs go on deterministic block lists.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按显式布尔条件即时判定的组件，零模型推理、可审计。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A rule engine decides instantly on explicit boolean conditions, with no model inference and full auditability.

scenario: 面试官问：都有 GBT 和 GraphSAGE 了，规则引擎为什么不是遗留包袱，还留着？
scenario_en: Interviewer: with GBTs and GraphSAGE in place, why isn't the rule engine legacy baggage — why keep it?
q: 规则引擎在 ML 之外承担哪些 ML 干不了的职责？(多选)
q_en: What jobs does the rule engine do that ML can't? (multiple)
why: 规则做 ML 做不到的三件事：即时确定性硬拦已知坏模式(零推理)、在模型重训/服务出错时兜住基线欺诈、提供可审计的显式逻辑满足监管。降低训练 GPU 成本不是规则的职责。
why_en: Rules do three things ML can't: instantly hard-block known bad patterns at zero inference cost, act as a safety net for baseline fraud during retraining/serving errors, and provide auditable explicit logic for compliance — lowering GPU training cost is not their job.
options: 即时硬拦已知坏模式(受制裁国家/失陷 BIN)，零推理成本
模型重训或服务出错时兜住基线欺诈的安全网
可审计的显式逻辑，满足监管合规
降低训练 GPU 集群的成本
options_en: Instantly hard-block known bad patterns (sanctioned countries/compromised BINs) at zero inference cost.
A safety net catching baseline fraud during model retraining or serving errors.
Auditable explicit logic satisfying regulatory compliance.
Lowering the cost of the training GPU cluster.
optionExplanations: 对；已知坏模式是布尔判定，规则零成本即时拦，还省下给这些交易跑 ML 的算力。
对；模型下线/漂移/推理报错时，规则是不依赖模型的最后防线，守住基线欺诈。
对；监管要能审计「为什么拒付」，显式规则可读可查，不透明概率满足不了。
错；GPU 成本是训练侧的事，和规则引擎在推理路径上的职责无关。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — known bad patterns are boolean checks the rule engine blocks instantly at zero cost, saving ML compute on them.
Correct — when the model is down, drifting, or erroring, rules are the model-independent last line holding baseline fraud.
Correct — regulators must audit why a decline happened; explicit rules are readable, which opaque probabilities aren't.
Incorrect — GPU cost is a training-side concern, unrelated to the rule engine's role on the inference path.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型失效期间仍能拦住基线欺诈的独立防线，不依赖 ML。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A safety net is a model-independent line that keeps blocking baseline fraud while the model is unavailable.

scenario: 打分管线里，规则引擎放在 GBT 之前作为预过滤器先跑。
scenario_en: In the scoring pipeline, the rule engine runs first as a pre-filter before the GBT.
q: 为什么规则引擎要排在 ML 之前，而不是之后？
q_en: Why does the rule engine run before ML, not after?
why: 规则先跑当预过滤：命中硬拦规则的交易直接拒掉、不再调用 ML→省下这些交易的推理算力、拉低平均延迟；剩下需要判断的才进 GBT。若放在 ML 之后，每笔都得先付一次推理成本，白算。
why_en: Rules run first as a pre-filter: transactions hitting a hard-block rule are rejected without invoking ML → saving their inference compute and lowering average latency, and only those needing judgment reach the GBT; after ML, every transaction would pay an inference first for nothing.
options: 顺序无所谓，规则放前放后最终结果和总成本都完全一样
规则该放在 ML 之后，只在模型拿不准的中间档再用规则复核
规则先当预过滤：硬拦命中直接拒、不调 ML，省下推理算力
规则放前面是为了给 ML 攒更多带标签的训练数据
options_en: Order doesn't matter; rules before or after give exactly the same outcome and cost.
Rules should sit after the ML, reviewing only the uncertain middle band the model can't call.
Rules act as a pre-filter: hard-block hits are declined without calling ML, saving inference compute.
Rules go first so the ML accumulates more labeled training data.
optionExplanations: 顺序影响成本：放前面能省掉被硬拦交易的推理，放后面每笔都白付一次，结果不等价。
复核确实有用，但把规则整体放最后就失去了预过滤省算力、降延迟的主要好处。
对；把确定的坏交易先便宜地拦掉，只让不确定的付更贵的 ML 推理，省算力又降平均延迟。
预过滤的目的是省算力和降延迟，不是攒训练数据，这个说法答非所问。
optionExplanations_en: Order affects cost: first, it saves inference on blocked transactions; last, every transaction pays for nothing — not equivalent.
Review is useful, but putting all rules last loses the main pre-filter benefit of saving compute and cutting latency.
Correct — cheaply block certain-bad transactions first so only uncertain ones pay costlier ML inference, saving compute and average latency.
The pre-filter's purpose is saving compute and latency, not accumulating training data — this misses the point.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在昂贵步骤之前用便宜判定先剔除一部分输入，省下下游算力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A pre-filter cheaply removes some inputs before an expensive step, saving downstream compute.

scenario: GBT 给一笔通过规则的交易输出欺诈概率后，系统按概率分档处置。
scenario_en: After the GBT outputs a fraud probability for a rule-passing transaction, the system acts by probability band.
q: GBT 概率输出后的分层阈值处置是怎样的？
q_en: What is the tiered-threshold handling after the GBT probability?
why: 分三档：<0.1 自动批准、>0.9 自动拒绝、0.1-0.9 送人工复核。阈值按业务对误报(FP)/漏报(FN)的容忍度调——怕打扰好客户就抬高拒绝线，怕漏欺诈就压低。
why_en: Three bands: <0.1 auto-approve, >0.9 auto-reject, 0.1-0.9 to manual review, with thresholds tuned to the business's tolerance for false positives (FP) and false negatives (FN).
diagram:
flowchart TB
  P["GBT 欺诈概率 p"] --> A{"分档"}
  A -->|p<0.1| Y["自动批准"]
  A -->|p>0.9| N["自动拒绝"]
  A -->|0.1≤p≤0.9| M["人工复核"]
options: 只有一个 0.5 阈值：高于就拒、低于就批，全程没有人工环节
所有交易一律送人工复核，模型输出只当参考不直接处置
<0.9 一律自动批准、>0.9 才送人工复核，没有自动拒绝档
<0.1 自动批准、>0.9 自动拒绝、中间档送人工复核
options_en: A single 0.5 threshold: above declines, below approves, with no human step anywhere.
Every transaction goes to manual review; the model output is advisory and never acts alone.
Below 0.9 auto-approve and above 0.9 goes to manual review, with no auto-decline band.
Below 0.1 auto-approve, above 0.9 auto-decline, and the middle band goes to manual review.
optionExplanations: 单一硬阈值把不确定的边界样本也强行二分，误报漏报都升高，不如留一个人工带。
全量人工复核既贵又慢，模型的价值就是自动处理掉两头确定的大多数。
缺了自动拒绝档，高置信欺诈还要人工，白白拖慢并放大风险敞口。
对；两头自动、中间交人工，且阈值随 FP/FN 业务容忍度可调，是标准的分层处置。
optionExplanations_en: A single hard threshold forces uncertain borderline cases into a binary, raising both FP and FN — worse than a review band.
Reviewing everything is costly and slow; the model's value is auto-handling the certain majority at both ends.
Without an auto-reject band, high-confidence fraud still waits for humans, slowing things and widening exposure.
Correct — auto at both ends, humans in the middle, thresholds tunable to FP/FN business tolerance — the standard tiered handling.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把正常交易误判为欺诈，代价是打扰或流失好客户。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A false positive (FP) flags a legitimate transaction as fraud, costing you good-customer friction or churn.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把欺诈交易误判为正常放过，代价是直接的欺诈损失。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A false negative (FN) lets a fraudulent transaction through as legitimate, costing direct fraud loss.

scenario: GBT 给某笔交易打出 0.55 的欺诈概率——既不敢自动放行，也不敢自动拒付。
scenario_en: The GBT scores a transaction at 0.55 fraud probability — too risky to auto-approve, too risky to auto-reject.
q: 0.1-0.9 这个中间档为什么送人工复核，而不是强行二选一？
q_en: Why send the 0.1-0.9 middle band to manual review instead of forcing a binary?
why: 中间档模型不确定：自动批准会放欺诈、自动拒付会误伤好客户，两种错都贵。送人工复核用人的判断换取更低的 FP+FN，代价是人工有成本、有延迟，所以只把不确定的窄区间交给人。
why_en: In the middle band the model is uncertain: auto-approve lets fraud through and auto-reject hurts good customers, both costly, so manual review trades human judgment for lower FP+FN, at the cost of headcount and latency — hence only the narrow uncertain band goes to humans.
tradeoff: 人工复核中间档(降 FP/FN 但有人力成本+延迟) vs 纯阈值二分(快省钱但边界样本易错)
whenOtherWins: 若人工复核产能有限、或交易额极小(误判成本很低)，可收窄中间档、直接按阈值二分，少打扰人工。
options: 中间档一律自动放行，先把生意做成，损失事后再追
中间档一律自动拒付，宁可错杀也不放过任何风险
把 0.5 当硬边界二分即可，中间档根本不需要人工介入
把模型不确定的窄区间交人工判断，换更低的 FP+FN
options_en: Auto-approve the entire middle band; close the sale now and chase losses later.
Auto-decline the entire middle band; better to over-block than let any risk through.
Just split at 0.5 as a hard cutoff; the middle band needs no human involvement at all.
Send the model's uncertain narrow band to humans, buying lower FP+FN.
optionExplanations: 全放行等于对不确定的都赌不是欺诈，漏报和损失上升，风险敞口失控。
全拒付会大量误伤好客户，误报飙升、体验受损，把不确定当确定处理。
0.5 硬边界把边界样本强行二分，正是误报漏报最集中的区间，不该省掉人工。
对；只把最不确定的窄带交人工，两头确定的仍自动，是成本与准确的平衡。
optionExplanations_en: Approving everything bets that every uncertain case isn't fraud, raising false negatives and losses — exposure spirals out of control.
Rejecting all hurts many good customers, spiking false positives and damaging experience by treating uncertain as certain.
A hard 0.5 cutoff forces borderline cases — exactly where FP and FN concentrate — so you shouldn't drop the human step.
Correct — sending only the most uncertain narrow band to humans while auto-handling the ends balances cost and accuracy.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把模型不确定的样本交人工判定，牺牲吞吐换更低的误报漏报。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Manual review routes model-uncertain cases to humans, trading throughput for lower false positives and negatives.

scenario: Stripe 跑数百条规则，它们能抓到 ML 因训练滞后漏掉的约 10-15% 欺诈。
scenario_en: Stripe runs hundreds of rules that catch roughly 10-15% of fraud the ML misses due to training lag.
q: 规则能抓到 ML 漏网的欺诈，根因是什么，体现了什么设计原则？
q_en: Why do rules catch fraud ML misses, and what principle does it show?
why: 根因是训练滞后：新攻击手法还没进训练数据，ML 一时学不到，但人可以立刻写一条规则挡住→规则补上了模型的时间盲区。这就是 defense-in-depth：每个组件覆盖别人的盲点。
why_en: The root cause is training lag: a new attack vector isn't in the training data yet so the ML can't learn it, but a human can write a rule to block it immediately, filling the model's time blind spot — that's defense-in-depth, each component covering the others.
options: 因为规则本身比 ML 更准，本质上可以完全取代 ML 模型
训练滞后：新攻击还没进训练集，人却能立刻写条规则挡住
因为 ML 只在夜间批量跑一次，白天的流量全靠规则顶着
纯属巧合，规则和 ML 抓到的其实是完全同一批欺诈交易
options_en: Because rules are simply more accurate than ML and could replace the model entirely.
Training lag: a new attack isn't in the training set yet, but a human can write a rule against it immediately.
Because the ML only runs as a nightly batch, so daytime traffic is carried entirely by rules.
Pure coincidence; rules and ML actually catch exactly the same set of fraudulent transactions.
optionExplanations: 规则不是更准而是更及时，它补的是模型学不到新模式的时间差，取代不了会学习的 ML。
对；规则能立刻编码新攻击、绕开训练滞后，正是纵深防御让各层互补盲区的体现。
模型是实时在线的，不存在只在夜间运行，这个前提就是错的。
两者恰恰抓不同的：ML 抓学过的模式，规则抓刚出现、还没进训练集的新攻击。
optionExplanations_en: Rules are timelier, not more accurate; they fill the model's lag on new patterns and can't replace learning ML.
Correct — rules encode new attacks instantly, bypassing training lag, exactly how defense-in-depth covers blind spots.
The model runs online in real time, not only at night, so the premise is false.
They catch different things: ML catches learned patterns, rules catch just-emerged attacks not yet in the training set.

termDefinitions.meaning: 新攻击出现到进入训练数据、被模型学到之间的时间差。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Training lag is the delay between a new attack appearing and it entering the training data for the model to learn.

scenario: 50ms p95 预算拆解：入口解析~2、规则~2、特征库查询~8(并行:行为3/速度2/设备2/图3)、GBT 推理~3、后处理~2、出口~2，共~19ms。
scenario_en: 50ms p95 budget: ingress parse ~2, rules ~2, feature-store lookup ~8 (parallel: behavioral 3, velocity 2, device 2, graph 3), GBT inference ~3, post-processing ~2, egress ~2, total ~19ms.
q: 这份延迟预算里，真正的关键路径瓶颈是什么？
q_en: In this latency budget, what is the real critical-path bottleneck?
why: 加总约 19ms、留约 31ms 余量。瓶颈不是模型推理(~3ms)，而是特征库查询(~8ms)——这是常见面试误区。所以优化重心在特征检索，而不是换更快的模型。
why_en: The total is about 19ms with ~31ms headroom, and the bottleneck is not model inference (~3ms) but the feature-store lookup (~8ms) — a common interview misconception — so optimization focuses on feature retrieval, not a faster model.
options: 瓶颈是 GBT 推理(~3ms)，该去优化模型结构、换更快的实现
瓶颈是网络出入口(~4ms)，该去优化传输层和序列化格式
瓶颈是特征库查询(~8ms)，而不是模型推理(~3ms)
每一档耗时基本一样，这条链路上根本没有主要瓶颈
options_en: The bottleneck is GBT inference (~3ms); optimize the model structure or swap in a faster implementation.
The bottleneck is network ingress/egress (~4ms); optimize the transport layer and serialization format.
The bottleneck is the feature-store lookup (~8ms), not model inference (~3ms).
Every stage costs about the same, so this path has no dominant bottleneck at all.

termDefinitions.meaning: 决定端到端延迟的最耗时步骤链，优化这里才真正降延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The critical path is the chain of steps that dictates end-to-end latency; optimizing it is what actually cuts latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 95% 请求的延迟低于此值，衡量尾部延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: p95 is the latency below which 95% of requests fall, measuring tail latency.

optionExplanations: 推理只占约 3ms，远不是拖慢链路的那一环，换模型救不了真正的瓶颈。
出入口各约 2ms，加起来都没有特征查询一项贵，不该优化在这里。
对；真正吃时间的是约 8ms 的那一步查询，该优化的是检索链路而不是模型。
各阶段耗时明显不等，特征查询单项就比推理贵一倍多，不是平均分布。
optionExplanations_en: Inference is only ~3ms, nowhere near the slowest link, so swapping models won't fix the real bottleneck.
Ingress and egress are ~2ms each, cheaper than the lookup step alone — not where to optimize.
Correct — the ~8ms lookup against the feature store is what eats the budget, so retrieval work is the fix, not the model.
Stage costs are clearly uneven; the slowest single step costs more than double inference, not a flat spread.

scenario: 特征库查询占了关键路径(~8ms)，你要在不炸 50ms 预算的前提下压住它的尾部延迟。
scenario_en: The feature-store lookup dominates the critical path (~8ms), and you must contain its tail latency without blowing the 50ms budget.
q: 有哪些手段压低特征库查询的延迟与尾部风险？(多选)
q_en: Which techniques cut feature-store lookup latency and tail risk? (multiple)
why: 三招：跨特征族并行查询(行为/速度/设备/图同时发，总延迟≈最慢一族而非之和)、连接池复用(免去每次 TCP 握手)、激进超时+回退默认值(某查询 >10ms 就用默认值，不让单点拖垮整体)。
why_en: Three moves: query feature families in parallel (total ≈ the slowest family, not the sum), reuse pooled connections (skip the per-call TCP handshake), and use aggressive timeouts with fallback defaults (if a lookup exceeds 10ms, use a default so one slow point doesn't drag the whole request).
options: 跨特征族并行查询(行为/速度/设备/图同时发)，不串行等待
连接池复用连接，避免每次新建连接的 TCP 握手开销
激进超时+回退：某查询 >10ms 就用默认值，不让单点拖垮整体
把 GBT 换成更大的深度模型来补偿特征查询延迟
options_en: Query feature families in parallel (behavioral/velocity/device/graph at once), not serially.
Reuse pooled connections to avoid a per-call TCP handshake.
Aggressive timeout + fallback: if a lookup exceeds 10ms, use a default so one slow point doesn't drag the request.
Swap the GBT for a bigger deep model to compensate for feature-lookup latency.
optionExplanations: 对；并行让总延迟约等于最慢的一族而非各族之和，这是把 8ms 压在预算内的主力。
对；连接池省掉每次新建连接的 TCP 握手往返，去掉一笔固定开销。
对；超时回退防止某个慢查询把 p95 拖爆，用默认值换取可控的尾延迟。
错；换更大模型只会加重推理延迟，与特征库查询这个瓶颈南辕北辙。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — parallelism makes total ≈ the slowest family, not the sum, the main way to fit 8ms in budget.
Correct — pooling removes the per-call TCP handshake round-trip, cutting a fixed overhead.
Correct — timeout fallback stops one slow lookup from blowing p95, trading a default value for bounded tail latency.
Incorrect — a bigger model only worsens inference latency, opposite to the feature-lookup bottleneck.

termDefinitions.meaning: 预建并复用一批连接，避免每次请求都做 TCP 握手。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Connection pooling pre-builds and reuses connections to avoid a TCP handshake per request.

termDefinitions.meaning: 建立 TCP 连接的三次往返，每次新建连接都要付这笔延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The TCP handshake is the round-trips to set up a TCP connection, a latency paid on every new connection.

scenario: 一笔交易进入欺诈打分服务，要在 50ms 内走完主路径给出处置。
scenario_en: A transaction enters the fraud-scoring service and must traverse the main path within 50ms to a decision.
q: 把一笔交易的欺诈打分主路径排成正确顺序：
q_en: Order the fraud-scoring main path correctly:
steps: 规则引擎先跑：命中硬拦规则直接拒、不调用 ML
按阈值分档：<0.1 批准 / >0.9 拒绝 / 0.1-0.9 人工复核
并行查特征库(含预计算的 GraphSAGE 嵌入)
why: 规则引擎先当预过滤挡掉已知坏交易→通过的并行拉取特征(含预计算图嵌入)→GBT 算欺诈概率→按阈值分档处置。把确定性、便宜的步骤放前面，只让需要判断的交易付更贵的计算。
why_en: The rule engine pre-filters known-bad transactions first → passing ones fetch features in parallel (including precomputed graph embeddings) → the GBT scores fraud probability → tiered thresholds decide, putting cheap deterministic steps first so only uncertain transactions pay costlier compute.
diagram:
flowchart LR R["规则引擎预过滤"] --> F["并行查特征库
含GraphSAGE嵌入"] F --> G["GBT出欺诈概率"] G --> T["阈值分档
批准/拒绝/复核"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 每笔请求实时必经的低延迟处理链，重计算要尽量移出这里。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The hot path is the low-latency chain every request must traverse in real time; heavy compute should be moved off it.

scenario: 主路径实测约 19ms，而 p95 预算是 50ms，刻意留了约 31ms 余量。
scenario_en: The main path measures ~19ms while the p95 budget is 50ms, deliberately leaving ~31ms of headroom.
q: 为什么要刻意留这 ~31ms 余量，而不是把预算用满？
q_en: Why deliberately keep ~31ms of headroom instead of using the full budget?
why: p95 预算是给定 SLO、不是算出来的；~31ms 余量留给尾部尖峰、重试、以及某个特征查询超时后回退的兜底动作。p95 下真实分布有长尾，留白才不会在抖动时集体超标。
why_en: The p95 budget is a given SLO, not derived, and the ~31ms headroom absorbs tail spikes, retries, and fallback after a feature-lookup timeout, since the real distribution has a long tail that would otherwise breach the SLO under jitter.
options: p95 是给定 SLO；余量留给尾部尖峰、重试与特征超时回退
余量就是浪费，应该把预算用满去上一个更大的模型
31ms 是链路上的固定网络延迟，本来就改不动，不算余量
余量只是个要背下来的数字，没有任何设计含义
options_en: p95 is a given SLO; the headroom absorbs tail spikes, retries, and feature-timeout fallback.
Headroom is pure waste; spend the full budget on a bigger model instead.
31ms is fixed network latency on the path that you can't change, so it isn't real headroom.
The headroom is just a number to memorize with no design meaning.

termDefinitions.meaning: 给定的延迟/可用性目标，是约束而非公式结果，用来倒逼架构与留余量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SLO (Service Level Objective) is a given latency/availability target — a constraint, not a formula result — that drives architecture and headroom.

optionExplanations: 对；SLO 是给定约束，留出的空间正是用来扛尾部尖峰和超时回退，不会被抖动一下子打穿。
把余量填满换模型精度，遇到尾部尖峰就没有缓冲，抖动一来直接破 SLO。
31ms 不是固定的网络开销，它是刻意留出的缓冲，不是没法动的常数。
留白背后是应对长尾抖动的设计考虑，不是一个孤立要背的数字。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — SLO is a given constraint, and the slack exists to absorb tail spikes and timeout fallbacks without breaching under jitter.
Filling the slack for more model accuracy leaves no cushion for tail spikes, so jitter would breach the SLO immediately.
31ms isn't fixed network overhead; it's deliberate slack, not an untouchable constant.
The slack reflects a deliberate design decision for tail jitter, not an isolated number to memorize.

scenario: 复述 GraphSAGE 在欺诈打分里的两趟服务方式。
scenario_en: Recall how GraphSAGE is served in two passes for fraud scoring.
q: 补全 GraphSAGE 两趟服务的关键参数：
q_en: Fill in the key parameters of GraphSAGE two-pass serving:
text: GraphSAGE 上线用两趟：异步每 {{5-15 分钟}} 重算嵌入写入{{特征库}}，打分时只做一次 {{KV}} 查询取预计算嵌入喂给 GBT，把 {{50-200ms}} 的重计算移出热路径。
text_en: GraphSAGE serves in two passes: an async job re-embeds every {{5-15 minutes}} into the {{feature store}}, and scoring does a single {{KV}} lookup of the precomputed embedding for the GBT, keeping the {{50-200ms}} recompute off the hot path.
why: 两趟把重的 2-hop 聚合(50-200ms)挪到异步预计算、在线只留毫秒查表；代价是新团伙有 5-15 分钟检测滞后，由规则引擎兜底。
why_en: The two passes move the heavy 2-hop aggregation offline and leave only a millisecond lookup online, at the cost of a 5-15 minute detection lag for new rings, covered by the rule engine.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按键取值的毫秒级查询，这里按账号取预计算的图嵌入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A KV (Key-Value) lookup fetches a value by key in milliseconds, here the precomputed graph embedding by account.

scenario: 调 LightGBM 时，你可以加树的深度和棵数换离线精度，但每加一点都吃进 50ms 的在线预算。
scenario_en: Tuning LightGBM, adding tree depth and count buys offline accuracy, but each increment eats into the 50ms online budget.
q: 该按什么来调 GBT 的深度和树数量？
q_en: What should govern tuning the GBT's depth and number of trees?
why: 按延迟预算调、不是只看离线精度：深度和棵数越多离线 AUC 越高但推理越慢，要在 50ms 预算内选能跑完的最优点。为多 0.1% 离线精度而超时，线上反而更糟。
why_en: Tune against the latency budget, not just offline accuracy: more depth and trees raise offline AUC but slow inference, so pick the best point that still finishes within 50ms — chasing 0.1% more accuracy at the cost of a timeout is worse in production.
tradeoff: 深/多树(离线精度高但推理慢) vs 浅/少树(推理快但精度略低)
whenOtherWins: 若是离线批处理欺诈复核(没有实时延迟约束)，就该纯按精度堆深度和棵数，延迟不再是约束。
options: 只按离线 AUC 调，深度和棵数越多越好，延迟根本不用管
按延迟预算调：选 50ms 内能跑完的最优深度与棵数
固定深度不调，只调学习率和采样率就足够了
按 GPU 显存调，显存越大就把树设得越深、棵数越多
options_en: Tune by offline AUC only; more depth and more trees is always better and latency doesn't matter.
Tune against the latency budget: pick the best depth and tree count that still finish inside 50ms.
Leave depth fixed and just tune the learning rate and sampling rate.
Tune by GPU memory — the more memory you have, the deeper and more numerous the trees.
optionExplanations: 只看离线精度会调出跑不进 50ms 的模型，上线超时比那点精度损失严重得多。
对；离线精度和推理延迟是一对取舍，实时服务必须在预算内选最优点，而非无脑堆深度。
只调学习率放弃深度/棵数这两个主要旋钮，既控不住延迟也调不到最优。
GBT 在 CPU 上跑、跟 GPU 显存无关，用显存来定树深是错误依据。
optionExplanations_en: Optimizing offline accuracy alone yields a model that misses 50ms; a production timeout dwarfs that accuracy gain.
Correct — offline accuracy and inference latency trade off, so real-time serving picks the best point within budget, not blind depth.
Tuning only the learning rate abandons depth/count, the main knobs, controlling neither latency nor the optimum.
GBTs run on CPU and don't depend on GPU memory, so sizing tree depth by VRAM is the wrong basis.

termDefinitions.meaning: ROC 曲线下面积，衡量分类器区分正负样本能力的离线指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AUC (Area Under the ROC Curve) is an offline metric of how well a classifier separates positives from negatives.
